items.title: Cutting a pseudo-coherent complex in two pieces after localizing, once a cohomology group is generated by its reduction at a prime
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement is a local splitting result for a pseudo-coherent complex: if at a prime the natural map from the cohomology to the cohomology of the derived fibre is surjective in some degree, then after inverting one element outside the prime the upper truncation becomes perfect with amplitude starting at that degree and the complex splits as the direct sum of its two truncations (statement lines 19743-19763). The proof analyses the fibre in the critical degree through the image and kernel subspaces, lifts bases of the three pieces, and uses the surjectivity hypothesis precisely to lift the middle family, after which a localization makes the lifted elements a basis and the relevant quotient finite projective, so that the splitting statement can be applied (proof lines 19765-19818). The degree bookkeeping that identifies the quotient with the cokernel of the differential is what makes the upper truncation perfect. The counted span refers three times, once inside this chapter and twice to other chapters, all carried as navigation stubs.

primary.label: author lemma environment with its own label lemma-better-cut-complex-in-two (canonical tag 0A1U), with the surjectivity hypothesis and the two conclusions (source lines 19743-19763)
